onboarding.subtitleIos:
WalkPoint reads steps, weight, and height from the Health app for more accurate daily calories.

Tap “Allow access” — in the system sheet, turn on steps, weight, and height for WalkPoint.
onboarding.subtitleAndroid:
WalkPoint gets steps, weight, and height from Health Connect.

First open Health Connect (button below), then tap “Connect steps” — choose WalkPoint and allow steps (and weight/height if offered).
onboarding.usePhoneSensorHint: Counts steps in the background without Health Connect (hardware sensor required).
onboarding.hintIos: If the sheet doesn't appear: Settings → Privacy → Health → Data Access → WalkPoint.
onboarding.hintAndroid: If WalkPoint isn't listed: force-close the Health Connect app from recents and open it again, then tap “Connect steps” again.
onboarding.hintSamsung: Samsung Health: link it to Health Connect in Samsung Health settings.
onboarding.healthConnectRequiredMessage:
To sync steps you need Health Connect.

Install it from Google Play.

howTo.title: How to connect steps
howTo.subtitleAndroid: WalkPoint uses Health Connect for step data on Android.
howTo.subtitleIos: WalkPoint uses Apple Health for step data on iPhone.
howTo.footerAndroid: If steps don't update, make sure your source app (Samsung Health, Google Fit, etc.) shares data with Health Connect.
androidSteps: Open Health Connect (install from Google Play if needed).
In WalkPoint tap “Connect steps” and select WalkPoint in the list.
Enable Steps access — and weight/height if available for better calories.
If you use Samsung Health: Samsung Health → Settings → Health Connect → enable step sharing.
iosSteps: In WalkPoint tap “Allow access” and enable steps, weight, and height in the sheet.
Or: Settings → Privacy → Health → Data Access → WalkPoint.
Enable Steps, Body Mass, and Height for WalkPoint for better calorie estimates.
You can add weight and height manually in Health if missing.
Done. Steps and body data will come from Apple Health.
